swing_ideas.text: Inverted head and shoulders with potential to break out with weekend strength in crypto. Not the most compelling candle on Friday but any movement with closes over 209.5 get more compelling on the long side.

Ascending triangle with moving averages below the breakout point. Any holds over 52.45 area should bring in the last pivot high as a target around 59.15. Looking for 68.75 if it runs beyond that and the broad market remains strong.

Base forming with an attempt at consolidation over the daily 200 SMA (green). Looking for breaks over 78.45 for thin structure retracement towards the 83.65 level. Mind the daily 50 (blue) as potential resistance.
Post earnings run is pulling back into the neckline of a rounded bottom. Looking for buyers to attempt 59 holds, or breakouts over the pivot high around 66.6 for followthrough to the 90 area.

sections: S&P weekly chart – Reasonable that after an 18.5% run, the market slows down to consolidate. Location is key. In this $25 wide range, bulls have the edge. Under $550, concerns increase. Over $575, this is no longer a down trend.
S&P daily chart – Its quite clear that markets are balanced over the last week and a half. On the daily timescale, a break from the box initiates new ideas. In the box expect chop.
S&P daily chart – Use the August 2024 Yen carry trade volatility as a template for how the trend reversed. Not identical, but if the balance breaks down, a higher low keeps the reversal underway.

S&P hourly chart – Pretty classic balance rules with all 5 outcomes in force. Would prefer to trade any of the higher low green dots you see here to align with higher timeframe strength, and bullish supporting evidence. Would be fine to trade shorts on the red dots, but not overstaying my welcome.
Market internals – Key question to ask and answer here is, "As the market balanced, was there a bearish exchange level divergence?" Answer? No.

Market profile – Two conflicting nuances here. Value and PoC lower on Friday, however price continues to hold the base of the spike from Wednesday's FOMC session. Likely stacks as neutral, and we revert to balance rules.
